newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close mixed on lack of momentum.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close mixed on lack of momentum.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed mixed on Wednesday as, for the second consecutive session, early gains induced by Wall Street's rise were erased by late profit-taking, brokers said.
The weighted index rose to an intra-session high of 8,714.28 in early trade, but closed 1.33 points or 0.02 percent lower at 8,614.78.
Turnover was a heavy T$186 billion.
The trading pattern mirrored that on Tuesday in which the index remained moderately higher for most of the session, only to finish 23.26 points lower on a lack of momentum.

The Dow Jones industrial average racked up its second biggest one-day gain ever on Tuesday, rising 135.26 points or 2.10 percent to 6,587.16 in a rebound that sent positive sentiment rippling across many Asian stock markets.
But in Taiwan, the boost proved to be short-lived.
"Taiwan's market is at a peak and therefore is very vulnerable to profit-taking," said Joe Chiou, analyst for Taiwan Securities Investment.
The local bourse, buoyed by expectations of a continuing economic recovery, has gained about 25 percent in 1997 alone.

Brokers added that bullish effect from Wall Street was limited because the Dow Jones rise did not focus on the electronic sector -- the sector widely seen as enjoying the best fundamentals out of all the industries in Taiwan.
Electronics rose a moderate 0.55 percent on Wednesday. But the heavily weighted financials dropped 0.14 percent.
Brokers said they expected the market to remain in a consolidation on Thursday.
